problems.title: Expected copy count is distinct from exact deduplication
problems.source_location: Figure 5 and Listing 1, PDF p. 7; Appendix J.1, PDF p. 17.
claim: The appendix retains each qualifying duplicate independently with probability \(1/c\), explicitly describing a probabilistic rule.
analysis: For target allocation \(m\), \(K\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(cm,1/c)\), giving \(\mathbb EK=m\) and \(\operatorname{Var}K=m(1-1/c)\). At \(c=2,m=1\), probabilities for \(K=0,1,2\) are \(1/4,1/2,1/4\). Thus the algorithm gives one expected copy, not exactly one in each group.
result: The probabilistic algorithm is internally consistent under its appendix description. No experiment is shown to rely on a deterministic one-copy guarantee, so this remains a scope clarification.
